# Charter — T15 Tool authoring and BYO (retrospective, 2026-11-28)

- **Project:** T15 "Tool authoring and BYO", track v2, ADM phase G, capability plateau, tranche 12, plan `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §12. The record's only linked issue is #86, closed by PR #666 (merge `a2ef9194eb2c`).
- **Sponsor:** the programme's sponsoring group, through the tranche-12 PI plan and the standing delegation `01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14`. Tranche 12's authorisation is not this pack's to give; the P0 package `project_in_unauthorised_tranche:T15` clears only on that authorisation.
- **Objective:** a tool generated from an OpenAPI spec or a BYO MCP server is published, called by a job, and bounded by its effect ceiling and the tenant approval policy (SPEC_V2 §12).
- **Scope:** toolkit import, remote-MCP discovery, tenant binding, publication approval and the promotion request. Out of scope are tenant code execution, a caller-supplied URL at call time, a second MCP server and a second OpenAPI reader.
- **Governance:** the pack is authored under the ADM phase-G retrospective route; the Board's contract and the Phase-G review are recorded through this pack, and the closure review is the project's published decision.
- **Acceptance:** measured by the seven A–D artefacts, the delivery contract, the Phase-G review, both declared outputs and the closure review; the receipt reads them at the pinned snapshot.

soaw.title: Statement of Architecture Work — T15 Tool authoring and BYO (retrospective, 2026-11-28)

body.assignment: The architecture work assigns T15 the tool estate's authoring front door: OpenAPI draft import, service-scaffold registration, remote-MCP discovery as a client, tenant-binding resolution in the broker and the promotion request. T13 owns the four tool aggregates and the call path; T14 imports the estate; T6 supplies service registration. This statement governs the retrospective record of a project the record marks closed and measured built, read at the 2026-11-28 snapshot under the standing delegation.
body.scope: In scope are the draft lifecycle on governed_asset(kind='tool_draft'), toolkits.import_openapi, toolkits.import_mcp, tool_authoring.draft/validate/test/review, tools.publish/retire, tool_bindings.create/update/retire and toolkits.promote, with the approval_policy extension for approver kind, count and expiry. Out of scope are tenant code execution, a caller-supplied URL at call time, a second MCP server, a second OpenAPI reader, a second control plane and any archived kag binding.
body.responsibilities: The programme architect authors this retrospective statement; the delivery team owns the code and the merged tests; the Architecture Board owns the delivery contract and its decision; platform security owns the review of egress, credentials and effect class; the programme manager owns the closure record. No role in this statement re-decides the build that PR #666 merged.
body.acceptance_criteria: The gate reads: a tool generated from a spec is published and called by a job; publication approval defaults to a human and is tenant-configurable; a BYO MCP server is bound, narrowed and audited; a tenant cannot exceed its effect ceiling. The refusals are part of the acceptance: an unbounded draft is refused, an undeclared class defaults to read, and a destructive tool needs a named approver.
body.contract: The delivery contract is this pack's delivery_contract: it names the commitments, the compliance route at the pinned snapshot, the Board's approval and the manifest acceptance/programme/T15.toml. It is approved under the standing delegation and does not reopen the delivered architecture.
body.retrospective: This is the retrospective record of a delivered project, not a plan for new construction. Its work is to place the authored artefacts, the register rows, the Phase-G review and the closure review the record lacks, and to reconcile the manifest with the record's closed status. It manufactures no new acceptance and claims no run of a retired command.

# Architecture Artefact Index — T15 (retrospective, 2026-11-28)

## Metadata

Type index, version 1, owner the T15 project (#86), reviewer the Architecture Board at the 2026-11-28 retrospective, phase A–D, plateau PSA–HLD, related project T15 in tranche 12. The index names the seven artefacts this pack creates and the order the standard seeds them in.

## Entries

- Stakeholder Map (Phase A, matrix): the six stakeholders and their publication, credential, ceiling, audit, version and tenancy concerns.
- Driver/Goal/Objective Catalog (Phase A, catalog): tenant tools without a platform release, under platform control.
- Requirements Catalog (Phase A, catalog): R-T15-1 to R7 with their carrying actions and merged test binaries.
- Solution Concept Diagram (Phase A, diagram): the nine derivation, dependency, realization and reuse edges from source document to audited call.
- Business Capability Map (Phase B, diagram): the front door, publication governance, binding and ceiling, credential sealing, call and audit, and promotion.
- Data Entity/Data Component Catalog (Phase C, catalog): the tool, toolkit, binding, call, draft, policy and secret rows.
- Technology Standards Catalog (Phase D, catalog): Postgres 18 RLS, one binary, rmcp as a client, openapiv3 parse-or-refuse, approval_policy and the four-rank Effect.

## Links

The index derives from the seven artefacts it names and is the document the close gate reads for the mandatory architecture-artifact category. Each artefact links to another artefact of the pack, so the set is a graph rather than seven orphans.

## Document

The artefacts are created by this pack through architecture.artifacts_create and linked through architecture.artifacts_link at the pinned 2026-11-28 snapshot. The source design is docs/plans/inception/T15/02-architecture-design.md; the delivered route is PR #666.

risk.title: OpenAPI 3.1 fidelity
risk.body: A 3.1 document the pinned openapiv3 2.2.0 cannot parse could import partially and leave a toolkit with missing operations. The design makes this a typed refusal and a 3.0 fallback, never a silent partial import.
risk.response: The parse-or-refuse fixture is the check; a 3.1 sample either imports with closed schemas or refuses with a typed error naming the unsupported construct.

risk.title: A binding could widen the ceiling
risk.body: A tenant binding that is checked before the job binding could make a read job call a write tool. The design resolves job then tenant and takes the minimum of job, tenant and operation effect; no field may raise it.
risk.response: Refuse the call before the destination when the minimum ceiling is below the tool's effect; the gate suite attempts the widening.

risk.title: The tool-as-action namespace could leak
risk.body: An import that wrote an action_registry row would turn a tenant toolkit into a platform action and bypass the publication gate. Import must write toolkit and draft rows only.
risk.response: The import path is checked to write no action row; the action registry count is the witness.

risk.title: MCP discovery could widen the bound subset
risk.body: Discovery that proxies the full remote list would make an unbound tool callable and defeat the narrowing. The import persists only the bound operations, pinned by source_hash.
risk.response: The unbound call is refused before the network and a drift is a new import plus a kata.

risk.title: A credential could reach the call ledger
risk.body: A tool_call that recorded the credential would put a secret in an audited row. The binding carries an alias and the call row has no credential field.
risk.response: The alias is resolved at call time and the tool_call schema carries no credential; the BYO test asserts it.

risk.title: The publication gate could be unconfigurable
risk.body: An approval_policy row for tools.publish requires the action name to exist in the registry. The action is registered, and the absent-row default is a person.
risk.response: The policy fixtures cover an absent row and a tenant waiver, and the publication test proves both.

issue.title: Promotion is a request, not an admin toggle
issue.body: toolkits.promote opens a kata or development request. No authoring action stamps a platform version, so a promotion returns requested rather than a new platform version. This is a design refusal, not a delivery gap.

issue.title: The V1 /tools surface is not evidence for T15
issue.body: The V1 /tools route is the legacy surface and is not evidence for the V2 authoring front door. The V2 evidence is the merged tool_authoring and byo_tools suites at PR #666.

assumption.title: T13's broker and tool tables are the base
assumption.body: The authoring front door extends T13's tool, toolkit, tool_binding and tool_call aggregates rather than forking them. The record marks T13 closed and the delivered route uses those rows.

assumption.title: T6's service registration path exists
assumption.body: A scaffolded service registers its own OpenAPI through T6's path; T15 does not add a second reader or a second registry. T6 is closed in the record.

assumption.title: approval_policy can carry the approver fields
assumption.body: The design adds approver kind, count and expiry as columns on approval_policy rather than a second policy store. The delivered route uses the single table.

dependency.title: T13 — the tool aggregates and broker
dependency.body: T13 owns tool, toolkit, tool_binding, tool_call and the call path. The record marks T13 closed in tranche 3; T15 reuses it.

dependency.title: T6 — the approval policy and service registration
dependency.body: T6 owns the approval-policy use and the service registration path. The record marks T6 closed in tranche 11; T15 reuses both.

dependency.title: P0 — the programme definition
dependency.body: P0 defines the programme, the tranches and the project row. It is closed in the record; T15's tranche 12 sits under it.

dependency.title: #86 — the delivery unit
dependency.body: Issue #86 is T15's delivery unit, closed by PR #666 at merge a2ef9194eb2c. The retrospective pack does not reopen it.

benefit.title: Less bespoke tooling
benefit.body: The authoring front door and the BYO binding make every service a job uses a toolkit: a tenant publishes a spec or a bound MCP subset instead of bespoke glue. The measure is the tool_call ledger's per-toolkit counts at the review.

benefit.title: Predictable delivery
benefit.body: The receipt, the tranche exit and the complete record set are the measurable half of predictable delivery: a tranche that cannot show a green receipt cannot be forecast. The measure is the receipt verdict and the exit at one snapshot sha.

delivery_contract.title: Delivery Contract — T15 Tool authoring and BYO (retrospective, 2026-11-28)

body.commitments: T15 delivers the tool authoring front door: import an OpenAPI document or a service scaffold into a draft, bind a remote MCP subset, validate and replay, publish behind the human-default approval gate, bind a job or tenant with the lower ceiling, audit every call as one tool_call, and promote through a kata or development request. No tenant code executes and no caller-supplied URL is called.
body.compliance: Compliance is judged at the pinned 2026-11-28 snapshot against the record, which marks the project closed and measured built, and against the design's eight acceptance scenarios. The merged suites are crates/actions/tests/tool_authoring.rs and byo_tools.rs at PR #666. The design's original commands named rbuild; rbuild was retired by the owner on 2026-11-20, so this contract records the GitHub-hosted preflight as the replacement and claims no run of a retired command.
body.approval: The contract is approved by the Board's architecture decision recorded through the Phase-G compliance review in this pack, under the standing delegation. The retrospective record restates the delivered contract; it does not ask the Board to approve a second time or to reopen the build.
body.manifest: The acceptance manifest is acceptance/programme/T15.toml. It pins the project's closed status and carries the fifteen gate checks the receipt reads; the pin states the record, and the gate text states the delivered acceptance with the closure review.
body.acceptance_at: Acceptance is read at the 2026-11-28 snapshot, the same snapshot the T15 receipt and the tranche-12 exit read. The receipt is the instrument: verdict green means every check passed at that head, and a green from an older head proves nothing about this one.
body.retrospective: This contract is retrospective: it records a project already delivered on main by PR #666 (merge a2ef9194eb2c). Its obligations are the authorships and reconciliations the record set owes, not new construction, and its completion is the green receipt on the manifest.

wbs_deliverable.title: Tool authoring and BYO — the spec→publish→call route, the tenant publication gate, the BYO MCP binding and the effect ceiling

review.findings: This retrospective Phase-G review records the level compliant for the record set it assesses under the standing delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14, and it names every open package this pack resolves or leaves standing rather than leaving them implicit. It clears contract_missing:T15 through the delivery contract and mandatory_artefacts:T15 through the seven A–D artefacts, the Statement of Architecture Work, the charter and both declared output bodies. It clears the four PMP packages — std-pmp-change-control-t15, std-pmp-project-baseline-t15, std-pmp-project-registers-t15 and std-pmp-project-wbs-t15 — through the charter, the scope, schedule and cost baselines the factory records, the five register kinds and the WBS deliverable carrying 8/5/8/8. It clears the three TOGAF packages — std-togaf-architecture-artifact-t15, std-togaf-compliance-review-t15 and std-togaf-phase-g-t15-g — through the seven linked artefacts, this review and the closure record. project_brief_output:
# Project Brief — T15 Tool authoring and BYO (retrospective, 2026-11-28)

## Outcome

A tool generated from an OpenAPI spec or a BYO MCP server is published, called by a job, and bounded by its effect ceiling and the tenant approval policy. The record marks the outcome delivered and measured built; this retrospective restates it for the authored set the close gate reads.

## Boundary

In scope are toolkit import (draft toolkit and tool rows), remote-MCP discovery as a client, tenant-binding resolution in the broker and the promotion request, all as toolkit rows rather than new actions. Out of scope are executing tenant code, a caller-supplied URL at call time, the agent platform's MCP server as a dependency, any archived kag component, a second control plane and a second OpenAPI reader.

## Reuse sources

The authoring front door reuses crates/actions/src/ingest.rs for OpenAPI parsing and the breaking-change diff, crates/actions/src/mcp.rs and rmcp for the streamable-HTTP client, migrations/0050_approval_policies.sql for the publication gate, migrations/0013_documents.sql for the alias-only credential store, and governed_asset for the draft lifecycle. No second reader, registry or policy table is created.

## Inception units

The project's inception analysis is published as `01a1ee5f-51f8-7613-8d20-35d470d53ecc` and its architecture design as `01a1ee5f-5b42-70c5-9c35-86f977d14e85`, both at 2026-11-21.
